# Introduction

In this tutorial, we will set up the essential tools required for doing data analytics using Positron, and R. The focus is on creating a working environment where you can smoothly install software, organise projects, load data, and generate reproducible results. By the end of this tutorial, you will be able to use both R and Python within Positron to write code, run analyses, and document your workflow. To practice these essentials, we will use the Gapminder dataset to create a simple visualisation that illustrate the relationship between health and wealth across countries.

# Learning objectives

By the end of this tutorial, you should be able to:

- Install and configure Positron, and R, ensuring your development environment is ready for analytics work.

- Create and organise a Positron project with folders such as data and img to keep your workflow structured and reproducible.

- Install and load key packages in both R (tidyverse) for data manipulation and visualization.

- Perform basic tasks—writing code, obtaining outputs, and taking notes—using three different approaches: the console, scripts, and Quarto documents.

- Apply these skills to a real dataset by filtering, visualizing, and annotating results in R.

# R essentials

1. Install Positron and R

2. Open Positron, and create a new project in Positron and create new folders such as data, img, etc 

3. Install packages , `tidyverse` 
   - `install.packages("tidyverse")`

4. Load packages, `library(tidyverse)`

5. Three main tasks in R when doing data analytics:

   - Write code
   - Get outputs
   - Take notes 

Perform three tasks in:

   - Using Console
   - R script
   - Quarto

In this tutorial, we will practice using the following code chunk:

```{r}
#| label: tasks-r
#| echo: true
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse) # Load the package tidyverse
gapminder <- read_csv("data/gapminder.csv")# Import data into R
gapminder_filtered <- gapminder |> # Filter data to show only observation for 2007
  filter(year == 2007)
ggplot(data = gapminder_filtered,#Create a plot
       mapping = aes(x = gdpPercap, y = lifeExp, #display variable gdpPercap in x-axis 
                     #and lifeExp in y-axis from gapminder_filtered data 
                     size = pop, color = continent)) +# assign different point size based on population of countries and assign different colors to different countries  
  geom_point()+#create a scatter plot
  labs(x = "GDP per capita", y = "Life expectancy",# cosmatic part pf the graph
       title = "Health and wealth are strongly related",
       subtitle = "142 countries; 2007 only", caption = "Source: The Gapminder Project",
       color = "Continent", size = "Population") +
  theme_classic()
```
